title: SWF Releases its July 2026 Newsletter
text:
Secure World Foundation has published its July 2026 Newsletter.
Secure World Foundation’s July 2026 newsletter is now available, with updates on space governance, security, sustainability, and upcoming SWF activities around the world.
This edition opens with a new Insight from SWF Executive Director Peter Martinez examining the pressures facing the United Nations Committee on the Peaceful Uses of Outer Space. The article looks at how COPUOS can respond to rising membership, geopolitical tensions, a growing agenda, and resource constraints while preserving consensus-based diplomacy.
The newsletter also highlights several major SWF initiatives. Readers can learn more about registration and university sponsorship opportunities for the 8th Summit for Space Sustainability in Brasília, the completion of all UN Member State profiles on the Space Security Portal, and a new report on verifying compliance with the Outer Space Treaty’s prohibition on placing nuclear weapons in orbit.
Additional updates include details on SWF’s upcoming orbital data centers panel in Washington, the 2026 Outer Space Security Conference in Geneva, the AMOS Policy Forum in Maui, and recent staff participation in workshops and policy discussions across Asia, Europe, and the United States.
Read the full newsletter for the latest from SWF and links to reports, events, and registration pages.

title: Speakers Announced for SWF Panel on Orbital Data Centers and Space Sustainability
text:
Secure World Foundation has announced speakers for “An Initial Conversation: Orbital Data Centers & Space Sustainability Implications,” taking place Wednesday, July 29, 2026, at the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace in Washington, D.C.
The event will examine the space safety, sustainability, and policy coordination questions raised by orbital data centers, or ODCs. These proposed satellite constellations are designed to support artificial intelligence and other compute-intensive applications by harnessing solar power in space.
Since January 2026, several U.S.-based prospective ODC operators have filed applications with the Federal Communications Commission. If fully deployed, these systems would add tens of thousands, and in some cases far more, satellites to low Earth orbit. That scale raises questions that go beyond routine satellite licensing and current operational practice.
The panel will include Ronald Birk, Principal Director, Space Enterprise Evolution Directorate, The Aerospace Corporation; Matias Cava, National Space Policy Lead, Policy, Advocacy, and International Division, Office of Space Commerce, U.S. Department of Commerce; and Jeff O’Neil, Director of Government Affairs, Planet Labs.
Alex Shi, SWF Senior Program Analyst, will moderate the discussion.
The event will begin with arrival and networking at 11:30 a.m., followed by the panel discussion at noon and a networking lunch.

title: Secure World Foundation: Secure World Foundation to Co-Organize the Outer Space Security Conference 2026
text:
Secure World Foundation is pleased to once again co-organize the Outer Space Security Conference 2026 (OS26) in partnership with the United Nations Institute for Disarmament Research (UNIDIR). The conference will take place Tuesday, 8 September, and Wednesday, 9 September 2026, at the Palais des Nations in Geneva and online.
This annual event brings together government officials, technical experts, civil society representatives, commercial leaders, and academics for candid, cross-sector dialogue on the evolving challenges facing space security.
Outer space is entering a renewed phase of strategic importance, defined by rapid innovation, growing competition, and deepening global dependence. As the domain becomes more central to critical infrastructure and commercial activity, questions about how space is accessed, used, and governed are becoming more urgent. At the same time, the dual nature of many modern space activities creates complex security dilemmas around destabilizing behavior, the role of new actors, and the strategic use of space data. These developments raise pressing questions about security and stability in orbit.
Against this backdrop, OS26 will provide a platform for meaningful exchange across policymakers, defence actors, industry, academia, and civil society. Through focused panel discussions on technical, legal, and policy dimensions, participants will explore practical pathways to strengthen the security and sustainability of outer space and help ensure that it remains stable and accessible for all.
Further agenda details will be added by UNIDIR in due course.
Event Details
Date: Tuesday, 8 September, and Wednesday, 9 September 2026
Location: Palais des Nations, Geneva, and online

title: Secure World Foundation Selects Dr. Anne-Sophie Martin as 2026 Space Sustainability Research Fellow
text:
Secure World Foundation is pleased to announce that Dr. Anne-Sophie Martin has been selected as a 2026 Space Sustainability Research Fellow.
Each year, SWF’s Space Sustainability Research Fellowship supports focused research on core concepts and policy questions that shape the long-term sustainability of outer space. The 2026 fellowship focuses on models for private sector participation in international governance for space safety and space traffic coordination.
Dr. Martin is a research assistant in international law at Sapienza University of Rome and a visiting researcher at the Institute for Innovation, International Law and Sustainability of the National Research Council of Italy. Her work focuses on international law and space law, with research experience in the protection of the space environment, lunar environmental protection, space traffic management, and the legal dimensions of dual-use space technologies.
She holds an LL.M. in space and telecommunications law from Paris-Saclay University and a Ph.D. in international law and space law from Sapienza University of Rome. She is a member of the Legal Council of For All Moonkind and a Senior Fellow at its Institute on Space Law and Ethics. She is also affiliated with the International Astronomical Union’s Centre for the Protection of Dark and Quiet Skies.
Since 2021, Dr. Martin has been a member of the Global Expert Group on Sustainable Lunar Activities, where she serves as Co-Chair of the working group on lunar environment protection. Since 2024, she has served as French Co-Chair of the AI and Space Law Society.
As an SWF Fellow, Dr. Martin will contribute research on private sector participation in international governance for space safety and space traffic coordination. Her final report and executive summary will be published on the SWF website after completion of the fellowship.

title: Secure World Foundation Hosts Initial Conversation on Orbital Data Centers and Space Sustainability
text:
Secure World Foundation hosted “An Initial Conversation: Orbital Data Centers & Space Sustainability Implications” on July 29, 2026, at the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace in Washington, D.C.
The panel examined the space safety, sustainability, and policy coordination questions raised by orbital data centers, or ODCs. These proposed satellite constellations are designed to support artificial intelligence and other compute-intensive applications by harnessing solar power in space. If fully deployed, current ODC proposals would add tens of thousands, and in some cases far more, satellites to low Earth orbit.
Speakers discussed how policymakers, regulators, operators, and the broader space community can assess these proposals without treating them as routine satellite licensing matters.
Several themes emerged during the discussion, including the need for trusted space situational awareness, stronger coordination between operators, system-level review of large constellations, and evidence-based study of atmospheric and reentry impacts.
“Coordination between operators is the key,” said Ezra Feilden, co-founder and CTO of Starcloud, noting that multiple uncoordinated operators in the same orbital regimes could create serious challenges.
Jeff O’Neil, Director of Government Affairs at Planet Labs, emphasized the need for “the right SSA that is trusted,” including better modeling of the space environment and international cooperation on SSA data sharing.
Ronald Birk of The Aerospace Corporation noted the need to examine how SSA capabilities and sensing infrastructure scale as ODC proposals develop.

title: Secure World Foundation to Participate in ITU Study Group 4 Working Party 4A Meeting | October 2026
text:
Secure World Foundation will participate in the International Telecommunication Union Study Group 4 Working Party 4A meeting in Geneva, Switzerland.
Ian Christensen, SWF Senior Director, Private Sector Programs, will represent SWF during the first week of the meeting. SWF is an associate member of Working Party 4A, which focuses on efficient orbit and spectrum use for the fixed-satellite service and broadcasting-satellite service.
Ahead of the meeting, SWF will prepare an input contribution to the Handbook on Sustainable Use of Orbit and Frequencies. The contribution will build on prior SWF submissions and will be coordinated across SWF program staff.
Christensen is expected to present the contribution during the Working Party meeting. SWF’s participation supports continued engagement on the sustainable use of orbital and spectrum resources and the international processes that shape satellite operations.

title: Ian Christensen to Participate in U.S. Space Forum in Vienna
text:
Secure World Foundation will participate in the Second Annual U.S. Space Forum, taking place October 15–16, 2026, at the Vienna International Centre in Vienna, Austria.
The forum is hosted by the U.S. Mission to International Organizations in Vienna and will focus on commercial space capabilities, innovation, and international coordination. The event is designed to provide international delegates with a better understanding of the U.S. approach to outer space law and policy, the U.S. domestic regulatory system, and the practical value of Artemis Accords principles.
Ian Christensen, SWF Senior Director, Private Sector Programs, will speak as a panelist in a session focused on COPUOS observers. His participation will provide SWF’s perspective on the role of non-governmental observers in international space policy discussions and the current and future challenges facing COPUOS.
The two-day forum is expected to include diplomatic missions in Vienna, COPUOS delegations, Artemis Accords signatory nations, U.S. government officials, commercial space representatives, and experts from academia.
Topics are expected to include space situational awareness, satellite manufacture and deployment, on-orbit servicing, the low Earth orbit economy, space resources, and lunar activities.

title: Ian Christensen will participate in the Global Space Traffic Management (GSTM) Workshop hosted by University of Edinburgh and Lockheed Martin
text:
Secure World Foundation will participate in the Global Space Traffic Management Workshop, hosted by the University of Edinburgh and Lockheed Martin from September 1–3, 2026, at the Royal Observatory Edinburgh in Edinburgh, Scotland.
The workshop will focus on expanding information sharing to support practical standards, best practices, and metrics for space traffic management. Discussions will examine how to broaden data and information exchange across national, coalition, and international civil and military space command and control frameworks.
Ian Christensen, SWF Senior Director, Private Sector Programs, will participate in the workshop. His participation will support SWF’s work on space situational awareness, space traffic coordination, and practical approaches for improving the long-term safety and sustainability of space operations.
The workshop will feature interactive, scenario-based discussions designed to produce community guidance on research and development, policy development, and the evolution of operational frameworks. Participants will also examine how shared insights can be translated into standards, best-practice guidelines, and measurable metrics that can be used across the global space community.
The workshop will also address outreach strategies to expose these resources to a wider audience and support effective uptake and implementation.

title: Victoria Samson to Participate in Lunar Security and Governance Tabletop Exercise
text:
Secure World Foundation will participate in a Tabletop Exercise on Lunar Security and Governance hosted by the Geneva Centre for Security Policy, in collaboration with the Open Lunar Foundation, on September 7, 2026, in Geneva, Switzerland.
The scenario-based exercise will explore how emerging lunar activities could create governance challenges under the Outer Space Treaty. Discussions will focus in particular on Article IV, which governs military activities in outer space, and Article IX, which addresses harmful interference, due regard, and consultation obligations between space actors.
As lunar exploration moves toward sustained infrastructure and long-term presence, many capabilities are expected to be dual-use. That can blur the lines between civil, commercial, and security-related activities. A growing number of actors near and on the Moon also raises practical questions about coordination, operational proximity, information-sharing, and dispute management.
Victoria Samson, SWF Chief Director, Space Security and Stability, and Almudena Azcárate Ortega, SWF Senior Program Analyst, Space Law and Regulation, will participate as subject matter experts.
The tabletop exercise will be preceded by “Lunar Security and Strategic Competition,” a public event in the GCSP Geneva Security Debate Series. That event will examine lunar security, governance, international space law, and the future of cooperation and competition on the Moon.
